ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown with two distinct, thin yellow lateral stripes running the length of the body. A dark nuchal collar and keeled scales distinguish the species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Hebius parallelus* is the presence of a distinct, thin, pale vertebral stripe running down the center of its back.
ai.habitat: *Hebius parallelus* typically inhabits moist, dense evergreen or broadleaf forests in the Himalayas, often found near streams at altitudes between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Striped Keelback is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for frogs and tadpoles in damp habitats near streams and marshes during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hebius parallelus* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Striped Keelback (*Hebius parallelus*) is found in Northeast India, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to elevations of approximately 2,000 meters.
